text:
sanjay: Quick sync — proposal to move a small subset of residency/sovereignty enforcement into a proxy sidecar that lives next to edge proxies. Goals: reduce control-plane roundtrips for common policy checks, do local prefetching of allowed-region lists, and short-circuit simple consent checks.

elaine: I like the latency angle. Clarify what "small subset" means — are we talking about only read-only hints (e.g., allowed regions + TTL) or full write-block decisions?

mike: Prefer read-mostly in the sidecar. Writes should still require control-plane handshake unless there's a hardened emergency rule. Sidecar keeps a decision cache with short TTL (30s–2m). That gives most requests a local decision while preserving central revocation.

alyssa: Two operational questions: 1) how do we roll out policy changes without causing split-brain enforcement, and 2) what's the memory/CPU cost per proxy? We already run small VMs at POPs.

sanjay: Answers: 1) rollout model — every policy change increments a monotonic policy_version. Sidecars subscribe to a lightweight SSE stream and apply diff patches. For critical revokes we push a policy_version_hint that forces immediate fetch. 2) cost — sidecar is tiny (~40–60MB heap, single-threaded async). We measured ~<1ms median added for the proxy path in bench env.

mike: Can we formalize the interface? Thinking gRPC with a tiny proto: CheckRequest { tenant_id, token, op, resource_region_hint } -> CheckResponse { allowed: bool, policy_version, reason }. Sidecar keeps local cache keyed by (tenant, op) and falls back to control-plane with backoff.

elaine: We need a safety valve: if sidecar can't reach control-plane for X seconds, either fail open or fail closed depending on tenant SLA/privacy tag. That implies the sidecar needs to be policy-aware about tenants' failure-mode.

alyssa: Also consider telemetry. If decisions are happening at sidecars we must ensure traces include policy_version and decision_source (sidecar|control-plane) to debug misroutes.

opsbot: deploy-bot: Canary group alpha-pop applied sidecar v0.1 -> 15 proxies OK, 2 timeouts resolved by increasing control-plane read timeout to 800ms.

sanjay: On the subject of sovereignty boundaries — sidecar should never store sensitive payloads. Only store policy metadata and region lists. All audit logs remain centralized; sidecar forwards minimal audit events (decision_id, tenant, policy_version) to the observability pipeline.

mike: Tradeoffs / risks I see: - Policy drift if SSE lags - Increased attack surface at POPs (we need a hardened attestation token for policy SSE) - More complex debugging when sidecars diverge from control-plane truth.

elaine: Mitigations: signed policy blobs with TTL + version, verify signature before apply. Add a control-plane endpoint to force-global-reload and an operator playbook that drains POP if it has stale policy.

sanjay: Example operator command (POC):
```bash
# force reload policies for tenant 42 across all sidecars
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/admin/tenants/42/policy/reload -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_API_TOKEN" -d '{"policy_version":"2024-11-02-045"}'
```

alyssa: For long-term refactor: if this proves stable, consider moving from SSE to a CRDT-ish gossip for region lists so proxies can self-heal during partition. But that's a bigger effort and has correctness costs — worth exploring after stable telemetry.

mike: Also a small note on token stamping: if we stamp the client token with policy_version at issuance, sidecars can immediately accept decisions without re-checking for that version. That reduces control-plane pressure but requires token revocation flow.

sanjay: Proposed immediate next steps: 1) ship a constrained POC sidecar with read-cache + signed policy blobs on canary POPs, 2) add trace fields policy_version and decision_source to request traces, 3) document operator rollback/forced-reload playbook. Anyone object?

elaine: +1 as long as the forced-reload playbook exists in runbooks and it's tested in chaos days.

alyssa: +1 — I'll add tracing PR and start sizing estimates for memory/CPU.

mike: +1 — I'll draft the proto and the signed policy blob format.

sanjay: Great. I'll create a short RFC follow-up describing the diffusion boundary, the control-plane SSE contract, and the operator commands. Tagging @devops and @security for the attestation and signing requirements. :thumbsup:
